Synopsis:
He is smarter than your average goblin, and is reading a manuscript - loose papers, freshly written by Volo. It's a study of goblin behaviour that would give anyone who reads it an advantage in combat against goblins.

Cluster Contexts:
- GOB_NerdyGoblinSage.json: Booyahg Piddle is an unusually literate goblin caught reading a freshly written Volo manuscript — a study of goblin behaviour that would give anyone who reads it a real edge against goblins in combat. The exchange likely happens in or near the Emerald Grove/tiefling camp after a recent goblin attack you helped repel, where makeshift training (and an uneasy sheltering of refugees) is underway. Off‑screen the druids are preparing a ritual to cut the grove off and tensions are high; Asharak-style trainees or other survivors may be nearby but not in the immediate exchange. The player has a reacting mark or ability (a glowing symbol) that stirs during the conversation, and can try intimidation or persuasion to take the manuscript — the goblin may cede it if scared or convinced.
- GOB_NerdyGoblinSage_AD.json: a goblin reading a book, and struggling to make sense of it
- GOB_VoloBallad_Volo_Massacre.json: Volo, a reknowned scholar, has been captured by goblins and is being forced to sing on a stage at their celebratory party following a raid. One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.
- GOB_VoloBallad_Volo_FestivitiesArea.json: Volo, a reknowned scholar, has been captured by goblins and is being forced to sing on a stage at their celebratory party following a raid. One goblin has the responsibility of guarding him and engages him in conversation. If the goblins are killed, he investigates the corpses, researching the cause of death.
- CAMP_GoblinHuntCelebration_Volo.json: Volo's dialog after the goblin hunt celebration party. Occurs whether tieflings or raiders win, with a variation for whether we've met Volo or not. This is his fallback in being added to our camp.In the tiefling victory variation, Volo is sitting at his desk and thinking/writing an account of our victory that day. As we approach he should set down his pen and turn to speak with us, only returning to work again once he's dismissed us.In the goblin victory celebration, Volo is standing in a cage much like the one in which he is placed in the goblin camp. In this case, he does not wish to be freed. He isn't writing anything or holding anything, but hands off his notes off-screen if intimidated into doing so.
